subtitle: Learn how to choose and apply the right scales over chord progressions for melodic lead playing.

introduction.title: The Scale-Chord Relationship
introduction.text: Understanding which scales work over which chords is the foundation of melodic lead guitar. By targeting chord tones and choosing appropriate scales, you can create lines that sound intentional and musical.

columns.title: Target Chord Tones
columns.text:
The strongest melodic notes are chord tones (root, 3rd, 5th, 7th). Land on these during chord changes to create harmonic connection.

C Major Chord (C-E-G):
Strong: C, E, G (chord tones)
Good: D, A (scale tones)
Weak: F, B (avoid notes)

columns.title: Key Center Approach
columns.text:
Identify the overall key of the progression, then use scales from that key while emphasizing chord tones.

Key of G Major:
G-Am-C-D progression
Use G Major scale/pentatonic
Target chord tones on changes

cards.title: Chromatic Approach
cards.description: Use chromatic notes to approach chord tones from a half-step above or below.

fields.label: Example
fields.value: To reach C (root), play C# or B first. To reach E (3rd), play F or D# first.

practiceSection.title: Scale Application Practice Method
items: Learn the Chords: Play through the chord progression slowly. Identify each chord's root, 3rd, and 5th on the fretboard.
Map the Scale: Choose your scale and practice it over the backing progression. Find where chord tones fall within the scale pattern.
Target Chord Tones: Practice landing on chord tones when chords change. Start with just root notes, then add 3rds and 5ths.
